subject: Request: SLA appendix — short-term quota elevation for XeroSys launch
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@xerosys.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@xerosys.com
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Short window quota elevation request for Dec 14 product launch

Hi Irene,

Quick note from procurement at XeroSys — we have a hard product launch week scheduled for Dec 14–16 and our usage projection through Redwood looks like it will exceed our current quota/fairness thresholds during a concentrated window (spikes in inference for user events and webhooks). Our SRE team is asking if Redwood can provide a short-term quota elevation + SLA appendix that covers: a temporary burst window for up to 72 hours, a clearly defined latency SLO for p90/p99 during that window, and an explicit fairness/exemption so we aren’t subject to automatic throttling during the peak.

We understand you have fairness policies and rate ceilings in place; this is a one-off event tied to a paid campaign (deal ID DX-2026-1142). Can you share what information you need from us to evaluate the request and a rough timeline for approval?

Attaching our launch plan & traffic curve for context.

Thanks —
Maria Gomez
Head of Procurement, XeroSys
Attachment: xerosys_launch_traffic.csv (csv)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@xerosys.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Short window quota elevation request for Dec 14 product launch

Hi Maria —

Thanks for the context and the traffic curve, that helps a lot. Short answer: we can usually accommodate a 72-hour burst uplift with an SLA appendix and a small one-time fee, provided there are clear guardrails (max sustained TPS, fallback model tiers, and monitored retry behavior). To move quickly I need:

- Confirmed start/end timestamps (UTC) for the window
- Expected p50/p90/p99 latency targets you want to see for the primary API route(s)
- Whether you require a hard throughput cap (we can do a soft uplift with rollback triggers, or a hard carveout)
- Billing contact for one-time uplift fee approval

I've attached a draft SLA appendix template that outlines an approach (temporary quota table, degradation/fallback policy, rollback conditions, monitoring hooks). Marcus will scope the technical feasibility for the particular model/route you use.

Proposed next steps:
1) XeroSys confirms timestamps + latency targets
2) Marcus replies with feasibility + any required runtime changes
3) We finalize appendix and route for signature (DocuSign) — target turn time 48 hours once we have the info

Attachment: XeroSys_SLA_Appendix_Draft.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of GTM Security & Escalations
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@xerosys.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 13:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Short window quota elevation request for Dec 14 product launch

Hi Maria —

Quick technical note: we looked at your traffic curve. A couple of implementation items to align on before we sign off on a hard uplift:

- Which model(s) are you serving in production for this campaign? CPU vs GPU variant matters for p99 guarantees.
- Do you need a strict fairness carveout (no throttles) or a prioritized lane (reduced throttling threshold with fallback to a cheaper model)? We generally recommend prioritized lane + fallback to avoid impacting other tenants.
- We will require a 24-hour pre-warm of capacity to reach expected kernel/jit steady-state; if you cannot provide pre-warm lead time we can still do it but we will limit the initial uplift for the first 6 hours.
- We can instrument a temporary elevated route that has explicit rate ceilings (e.g., 5x baseline for 72 hours) and automated rollback if error rates or latency regress beyond agreed thresholds.

If XeroSys confirms the model names and timestamps, I’ll update the appendix with exact numbers (TPS caps, p90/p99 targets) and the pre-warm requirement.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@xerosys.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@xerosys.com
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 08:09:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Short window quota elevation request for Dec 14 product launch

Irene / Marcus —

Thanks, all. Confirming the uplift window: 2026-12-14T00:00:00Z to 2026-12-16T23:59:59Z (72 hours). Primary model: xs-chat-v2 (GPU). Desired latency targets for the uplifted route: p90 <= 350ms, p99 <= 850ms. We want a prioritized lane (no hard block) with fallback to xs-chat-v2-quantized if load requires it. We can accept the pre-warm requirement and will provide a 36-hour lead for the pre-warm.

Procurement has run our signatures by legal and returned a few minor redlines to the appendix (mainly around measurement window and the rollback notification cadence). See attached redlines PDF; legal is OK with a one-time uplift fee — please provide the billing contact and quote.

Attachment: redlines_xerosys_sla_appendix.pdf (pdf)

Thanks —
Maria Gomez
Head of Procurement, XeroSys
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@xerosys.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 15:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Short window quota elevation request for Dec 14 product launch — approved with conditions

Hi Maria,

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the redlines. We reviewed the requested targets and redline items — we are comfortable approving a 72-hour prioritized lane uplift under the following conditions:

1) Uplift window: 2026-12-14T00:00:00Z — 2026-12-16T23:59:59Z (as requested)
2) Route: /v1/generate (mapped to xs-chat-v2), temporary capacity set to 5x baseline TPS during the window
3) Latency SLOs during uplift: p90 <= 350ms, p99 <= 850ms (measured at Redwood edge)
4) Pre-warm: XeroSys to confirm 36-hour pre-warm start by Dec 12 00:00:00Z; otherwise uplift will be limited for the first 6 hours
4) Fairness policy: prioritized lane (reduced throttling probability) with automatic, documented fallback to xs-chat-v2-quantized when error rate > 2.5% or p99 > 1100ms for a 5-minute sliding window
5) Monitoring & notifications: we will share a temporary dashboard and will notify your SREs if rollback triggers hit; rollback cadence in the appendix is set to "immediate" plus a 15-minute follow-up report
6) Fee: one-time uplift fee — quote sent to billing@xerosys.com (Marcus to include exact amount), invoice due net-30

I have uploaded the finalized appendix and initiated the DocuSign envelope for signatures. Marcus — please confirm the fee/quote and whether the pre-warm capacity needs any specific model-variant pins.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/transactions/0A12B3C4D5
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/1142

Attachment: XeroSys_SLA_Appendix_Final.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of GTM Security & Escalations, Redwood Inference
